brahman.why_not: A caste/metaphysical term, heavily loaded; also a cattle breed in the USA.

maga.why_not: Reads as 'MAGA' in the USA — politically loaded and disqualifying.

matila.why_not: The -ila ending reads feminine in English (Matilda); meaning is only 'a king's name'.

matsya.why_not: Means 'fish'; the ts-y cluster is hard and the meaning invites teasing.

madin.why_not: Core sense is 'intoxicating'; also collides with the Arabic-sounding Madin/Medina.

madra.why_not: A region/tribe name, and too close to Madras/Madre; not a personal name.

madgu.why_not: A cormorant/diver bird; awkward dg cluster and no appeal as a name.

manoka.name: Manoka
manoka.meaning: Name of a Sanskrit poet recorded in the catalogues
manoka.say_note: Three open syllables, stress falls naturally on the clear 'NOH'.
manoka.collisions: Evokes the familiar 'manas/mano-' (mind) family; no popular clash.
manoka.note: Value is as an attested poet's name plus the pleasant mano- (mind) resonance.

malaya.why_not: Reads as Malaya/Malaysia in the USA; also commonly a girl's name spelling (Malaya).

malla.why_not: Widely a surname/dynasty name and a caste-linked term for wrestler; also reads like 'Molly'.

mahin.name: Mahin
mahin.meaning: Great, mighty — a Rigvedic epithet of greatness
mahin.say_note: Simple and read correctly; no aspirated cluster (the h is a plain h).
mahin.collisions: Some overlap with Persian/Urdu 'Mahin'; uncommon among Indian-American boys.
mahin.note: 'Mahi' as a nickname reads slightly unisex in India.

matu.why_not: A technical musicology term; also reads as 'mother' (mAtR) to Indian ears.

macha.why_not: Reads as 'macho'/'matcha' in American English; lexical word for 'road'.

mayin.why_not: Means cunning, deceptive, illusory — negative meaning.

masika.why_not: Refers to a funeral oblation for the dead; also reads feminine.

mahaki.why_not: Obscure patronymic of a teacher; sounds foreign to both cultures.

mishra.why_not: Reads as the very common surname Mishra, not a first name.

muku.why_not: Artificial lexicographers' word; sounds like baby-talk in English.

mukta.why_not: Mukta is used as a girl's name (pearl) in Marathi.

mekala.why_not: Close to Mekhala, a feminine word (girdle); reads feminine.

metri.why_not: Reads as English 'metric/metry'; awkward as a name.

maitri.why_not: Maitri is widely used as a girl's name (friendliness).

mocha.why_not: Reads as the English coffee drink 'mocha'.

mochin.name: Mochin
mochin.say_note: Spelling is read correctly: MOH-chin; no aspirates or retroflexes.
mochin.collisions: Slight echo of 'Mochi' the dessert; otherwise unused.
mochin.note: Rare vocabulary word with a clean, positive meaning of liberation.

yajna.why_not: Cluster 'jn' is mangled by Americans; also a ritual word, not a personal name.

yati.why_not: Commonly means ascetic/monk and is used as a girls' name too; also reads 'yeti'.

yantur.name: Yantur
yantur.say_note: YAHN-toor; no aspirates, though the -tur ending may be said 'ter'.
yantur.note: Vedic word for one who guides; strong, unused, masculine.

yayi.why_not: Two-vowel name reads as a shout ('yay'); too slight.

yayu.why_not: Attested only in a corrupted passage; sounds like baby-talk.

yava.why_not: Means barley/half-month; weak meaning and reads like 'java'.

yatu.why_not: Yatu also means sorcery/demon in Vedic usage — negative.

yatri.why_not: Yatri means 'traveller/pilgrim' in everyday Hindi (bus announcements) — reads as a common noun.

yuvat.name: Yuvat
yuvat.note: Crisp Vedic adjective meaning young; unused and easy to say.

ranaka.why_not: Three syllables ending -aka reads feminine/awkward; obscure king's name.

raya.name: Raya
raya.meaning: river current, flowing stream, swift motion
raya.collisions: Raya is a girl's name in Slavic/Hebrew use and a Disney character; mildly unisex.
raya.note: Real Sanskrit word for a river's current; smooth with Gawande.

rayi.name: Rayi
rayi.meaning: wealth, treasure, prosperity (often personified in the Rigveda)
rayi.say_note: RAH-yee; may be read 'RAY-ee' by some.
rayi.collisions: Similar to Hebrew Rayi; not used among Indian-Americans.
rayi.note: Vedic word for treasure; unusual and positive.

ravija.name: Ravija
ravija.collisions: Echoes common Ravi but is distinct; note it also denotes Saturn.
ravija.note: Literally 'born of the sun'; rare as a given name.

rasa.why_not: Everyday word for juice/flavour; also 'rasa' reads oddly in English.

rati.why_not: Rati is the goddess of love, a female name; also reads 'ratty'.

rajoka.why_not: Obscure poet's name; first syllable suggests 'rajo-' dust/passion, awkward.

ruksha.why_not: Ruksha in Hindi/Marathi means rough, dry, harsh — negative.

rumra.why_not: Cluster -mr- is hard for Americans and sound is unattractive.

ruruka.why_not: Repetitive syllables sound comical in English.

ruvu.why_not: Means castor-oil plant; weak meaning and Dravidian-sounding form.

ruhvan.why_not: 'hv' cluster is unpronounceable from the spelling for Americans.

rohaga.why_not: Awkward-sounding obscure mountain name; no appeal.

rohi.why_not: Means a kind of deer; too close to common Rohit/Rohan and reads feminine.

rohita.why_not: Essentially Rohit, a very common name for men born 1950–1995.

lasa.why_not: Too slight and reads as 'Lassa/lasso'; weak.

leshya.name: Leshya
leshya.say_note: LESH-yah; the -shya may need one correction but is guessable.
leshya.note: Rare, soft-sounding word; acceptable but less strong than others.

lokin.name: Lokin
lokin.meaning: possessing a world, attaining the highest world
lokin.say_note: LOH-kin; spelled exactly as read, no tricky sounds.
lokin.collisions: Resembles Western Logan/Loki but is clearly distinct.
lokin.note: Upanishadic word; sounds modern and crisp with Gawande.

loga.why_not: Means a clod of earth or lump of clay — weak, unflattering meaning; also reads like 'logger'.

vakmya.why_not: A gerundive grammatical form ('to be praised'), and the -kmy- cluster is unpronounceable for Americans.

vagnu.why_not: Means an animal cry or roar; the -gn- cluster reads awkwardly and the meaning is not name-worthy.

vana.why_not: Reads as a feminine name in the USA and is a very familiar common word (forest); too plain.

vatu.why_not: Lexicon-only word; sounds like 'what to' in American speech and invites teasing.

vani.why_not: Vani is well established as a girl's name (speech/Saraswati) in India; clearly feminine.

vapra.name: Vapra
vapra.meaning: A rampart or raised earthwork; the firm foundation on which a building stands
vapra.say_note: Two clean syllables; only risk is Americans saying VAP-ruh with a flat 'a', which is acceptable.
vapra.collisions: No common name collisions; distinct from Vapur/Vipra.
vapra.note: Solid, masculine, unused; meaning of foundation and fortification is defensible and positive.

vami.why_not: Lexicon-only word for fire; sounds feminine and close to 'vomit'-like teasing (vami also means vomiting in Ayurveda).

vayya.why_not: Nice meaning (friend) but the double-y spelling makes Americans read 'VY-uh/via', and it resembles South-Indian 'ayya' forms.

vara.why_not: Everyday word (boon, bridegroom); far too plain and also used as a girl's name element.

varuna.why_not: A major established deity name and far too close to Varun, extremely common for Indian men born 1960–1995.

varni.why_not: Means a fragrant ointment (lexicon only); trivial meaning and reads feminine.

varmi.why_not: Means a kind of fish; unusable meaning and sounds like 'wormy'.

varshu.name: Varshu
varshu.meaning: Born of the rain; enduring, lasting like the monsoon
varshu.say_note: Spelling maps directly: VAR-shoo. No aspirates or retroflex traps.
varshu.collisions: Distinct from Varsha (girl) and Varun; the -shu ending keeps it clearly masculine.
varshu.note: Fresh, easy, evocative of the monsoon; not in use among Indian-American babies.

valla.why_not: Means a kind of wheat; trivial, and reads like a truncated Spanish/Italian word.

vashin.name: Vashin
vashin.meaning: One who has mastery; self-possessed ruler, lord of his own will
vashin.say_note: Reads cleanly as VAH-shin; Americans handle -shin easily.
vashin.collisions: Not to be confused with Vasin/Vashi; no popular-name collision.
vashin.note: Strong virtue meaning (self-control, authority), masculine -in ending, unused as a given name.

vastri.name: Vastri
vastri.meaning: The illuminator; one who makes things shine, bringer of daybreak light
vastri.say_note: VAHS-tree; the -str- cluster is familiar to English speakers.
vastri.note: Agentive noun used in Vedic compounds for 'illumining the dawn'; a genuinely rare light name.

vasyas.why_not: A comparative grammatical form ('better than'); the final -s makes it unusable as a name.

vati.why_not: Lexicon-only word for wind; slight and reads feminine, and echoes Hindi 'vaati'.

vatri.name: Vatri
vatri.meaning: The blower; the wind itself, the moving air
vatri.say_note: VAH-tree; the single t is not an English 'th' trap, and stress falls naturally on the first syllable.
vatri.collisions: No name collisions; distinct from Vatsa or Vitri.
vatri.note: Agent noun from vāta (wind); clean sound, elemental meaning, completely unused.

vatoka.why_not: Obscure poet's name; four-beat shape reads oddly in English and resembles a brand name.

vatya.why_not: Grammatical adjective ('being in the wind'); vātyā also means a windstorm and is feminine.

vagda.why_not: A ritual-formula adjective, not a name; the -gd- cluster is unpronounceable for Americans.

vajin.name: Vajin
vajin.meaning: Swift and strong one; a hero or warrior, full of vigor
vajin.say_note: VAH-jin reads directly from the spelling; no aspirates.
vajin.collisions: Close in sound to Vajra/Vijay but distinct; not in current use.
vajin.note: Vedic epithet of Indra and Agni for strength and swiftness; crisp, masculine, unused.

vadira.why_not: An obscure tree of uncertain identity; meaning too thin, and it reads feminine.

vasava.name: Vasava
vasava.meaning: Chief of the Vasus; an epithet of Indra, lord of the shining ones
vasava.say_note: Three open syllables, all simple consonants; Americans read it correctly on sight.
vasava.collisions: Vasava is a surname/community name in Gujarat, but rare as a first name; not a popular baby name.
vasava.note: Classical epithet of Indra; dignified and almost unheard of as a given name in the US.

vigra.name: Vigra
vigra.meaning: Strong and vigorous; by Vedic gloss, one of keen intelligence
vigra.say_note: VIG-ruh; both clusters are ordinary English sounds.
vigra.collisions: Distinct from Vigraha/Vikram; no baby-name collisions.
vigra.note: Rare Rigvedic adjective glossed as vigorous and wise — a compact, masculine, unused option.

vitula.why_not: A minor epic prince whose name is likely a scribal variant of Vipula; also reads like Latin 'vitula' (heifer).

vidu.name: Vidu
vidu.say_note: VEE-doo is unambiguous from the spelling.
vidu.collisions: Related to Vidur/Vidya but clearly its own name; Vidu is not in use for babies.
vidu.note: Short, warm and easy; the vid- root for knowing is instantly legible to Marathi family.

vidupa.why_not: Obscure king's name, and the '-dupa' segment invites teasing in English.

vidus.why_not: Stem form ending in -s; unusable shape for a name and would be read as 'videos/Vidus'.

vipa.name: Vipa
vipa.meaning: A learned man; one inspired with wisdom and insight
vipa.say_note: VEE-pah; two open syllables, no traps.
vipa.collisions: No collision with popular names; distinct from Vipul.
vipa.note: From the vip- root for inspired trembling/seer-poet; short and genuinely unused, though very brief.

vipina.name: Vipina
vipina.meaning: A forest or grove, stirring in the wind
vipina.say_note: Reads as vih-PEE-nah; risk is being heard as the female name Vipina/Vipin variant.
vipina.collisions: Vipin is a common older-generation men's name; Vipina is distinct but adjacent — parents may prefer to note this.
vipina.note: Beautiful classical word for a wind-stirred grove; flows well with Gawande.

vimata.why_not: Vimata as a word means 'disliked, of a differing opinion' — negative meaning despite the place-name use.

vista.why_not: Reads as the English word 'vista' (and Windows Vista); meaning is a unit of weight.

vrinta.why_not: Means a caterpillar or crawling creature; unusable meaning.

vegin.why_not: Good meaning (swift) but Americans will read 'VEE-jin' or hear 'vegan/Vegas'; pronunciation risk is too high.

vetra.why_not: Means a cane or reed (also the usher's staff); thin meaning and reads like a pharmaceutical brand.

vela.why_not: Reads as a Spanish/feminine name (vela = candle/sail) and velā in Sanskrit is a feminine noun for time/shore.

vaina.why_not: Denotes a mixed-caste occupational group — caste-loaded and inappropriate; also reads as a girl's name.

vaida.why_not: Reads as the common surname Vaidya/Vaid; not used as a given name

vaidya.why_not: A well-known Marathi surname and the word for 'doctor'; unusable as a first name

vyamla.why_not: Means 'free from acidity' — a medical term, faintly comic

vyarka.why_not: Means 'with exception of the sun' — a grammatical/astrological qualifier, no name value

vyakta.why_not: Primarily means 'manifest, explicit'; the vy- plus -kt cluster is mangled by Americans

vyapva.why_not: Unpronounceable -pv- cluster and a doubtful lexicon-only word

vraja.why_not: Too close to the already common name Vraj/Braj; also reads as a place name

vratya.why_not: Homophonous with vrātya, 'one outside the vows/outcaste' — risky meaning

shamsa.why_not: Reads as Arabic Shams/Shamsa and sounds feminine in English

shakna.why_not: Clunky -kn- cluster, lexicon-only gloss, no name feel

shakri.name: Shakri
shakri.say_note: Two clean syllables; Americans read it correctly, just watch for 'SHAK-ree'
shakri.collisions: Echoes Shakti/Shakira faintly but is distinct
shakri.note: A rain-cloud word — fresh, short, and easy on American ears.

shaka.why_not: Gloss is only 'a kind of animal'; also reads as Zulu king Shaka and the word 'shaka'

shadri.name: Shadri
shadri.say_note: Simple CVC-CV; no aspirates or retroflexes
shadri.note: Another rain-cloud word; unusual but instantly sayable.

shani.why_not: Saturn, considered inauspicious; also a Hebrew girl's name

shama.why_not: Shama is used as a girl's name (lamp/candle in Urdu); reads feminine

shamba.name: Shamba
shamba.say_note: Read exactly as spelled; no tricky sounds
shamba.collisions: Samba the dance; Shamba is also a son of Krishna in the Puranas
shamba.note: Warm, cheerful meaning with a Puranic echo; the 'samba' association is mild.

shasha.why_not: Means 'hare'; reads as the girl's nickname Sasha

sharga.why_not: Vague 'kind of bird'; sounds harsh and surname-like

shava.why_not: In Marathi/Hindi śava means 'corpse' — fatal association

shiksha.why_not: Everyday word for 'education/punishment' and used as a girl's name

shigru.why_not: Means horse-radish/drumstick tree; unattractive and odd-sounding

shinga.why_not: Marathi 'shing' means horn; reads as slang-adjacent and comic

shirin.why_not: Reads as the Persian feminine name Shirin; means only a kind of grass

shilin.name: Shilin
shilin.say_note: Spelling gives the sound directly; rhymes with 'feelin'
shilin.collisions: Can read as an East Asian name; related to common word 'sheel'
shilin.note: Clean virtue meaning from the familiar root sheel (character), yet essentially unused.

shukla.why_not: A very well-known North Indian surname

shunga.why_not: Dynasty name with doubtful etymology; awkward sound in English

shurna.name: Shurna
shurna.say_note: Read as SHOOR-na; the -rn- is easy, though some may say SHUR-na
shurna.note: Solid 'steadfast' meaning with an audible link to shoora, valiant.

sheva.why_not: Reads as Hebrew Sheva/Sheba and as Hindi seva; feminine in English

shravas.name: Shravas
shravas.say_note: Initial shr- takes a beat but Americans manage it (cf. 'shrub'); ends cleanly
shravas.collisions: Related to common Shravan/Shravani, but the -as form is unused
shravas.note: Vedic word for sound and glory; masculine and distinctive.

shrida.name: Shrida
shrida.say_note: SHREE-da; spelling is transparent, though a few may read 'Shrida' as 'Shrieda'
shrida.collisions: Close to the feminine Shridha/Sridevi sound world
shrida.note: Giver-of-prosperity; masculine in grammar but the -a ending is slightly soft.

shripa.why_not: Reads oddly in English ('shree-pa') and the gloss is a technical epithet

shrika.why_not: Only 'a kind of bird'; too close to Shrikant/Shreya and sounds feminine

shrenya.name: Shrenya
shrenya.meaning: name of a Buddhist king (Shrenika); of the noble rank/order
shrenya.say_note: SHREN-ya reads straight off the page
shrenya.collisions: Close in sound to the popular girls' name Shreya
shrenya.note: A real royal name from Buddhist tradition; crisp and unused for boys.

shlila.why_not: Inevitably read against ashleel ('obscene'); shl- cluster is hard

sadvat.why_not: Purely a ritual-grammatical term about verses; no name value

sata.why_not: Means a sacrificial vessel; reads as 'satta' and is flat as a name

santya.name: Santya
santya.say_note: SAHN-tya; the -tya is easy, like 'Satya' which Americans manage
santya.collisions: Close to Satya and to Marathi nickname 'Santya' for Santosh
santya.note: Rigvedic epithet of generosity; sound is familiar without being a used name.

sanaga.why_not: Three flat syllables, obscure teacher's name, reads like 'Saga/Sanaga' nonsense

sanaru.name: Sanaru
sanaru.meaning: name of an ancient Vedic teacher
sanaru.say_note: Fully phonetic; every syllable is open and easy
sanaru.collisions: No common collisions; faint echo of 'Sanjaru'-type sounds
sanaru.note: A genuine Shatapatha Brahmana teacher's name — a real name, yet essentially unheard today.

saya.why_not: Grammatical term meaning 'with the letter ya'; no real meaning as a name and reads feminine.

sarka.name: Sarka
sarka.say_note: Reads phonetically; rhotic R is natural for Americans.
sarka.collisions: Close to Czech name Šárka (female) but spelled differently in the USA.
sarka.note: Simple two-syllable nature word; pairs cleanly with Gawande.

sahra.why_not: Reads as 'Sahara'/'Sarah' to Americans; ambiguous and feminine-sounding.

sahvan.why_not: The -hv- cluster is unpronounceable from the spelling for Americans.

sakoka.why_not: Obscure poet's name; 'koka' element is awkward and the word sounds comic in English.

sagni.why_not: A ritual grammatical form ('together with the fire'), not a name; also hard to say.

sajoka.why_not: Obscure poet's name with no transparent meaning; sounds invented and odd.

suketu.name: Suketu
suketu.meaning: one with a bright banner or clear intelligence; name of a king
suketu.say_note: All open syllables, no clusters; Americans read it correctly.
suketu.collisions: Rare among Indian-Americans; not a 1950–95 generation staple.
suketu.note: Genuine epic name, still uncommon in the USA.

sutoya.name: Sutoya
sutoya.meaning: having fine water; name of a king
sutoya.say_note: Fully phonetic; slight risk of stress on first syllable.
sutoya.collisions: Essentially unused as a given name today.
sutoya.note: Water imagery, gentle sound, clearly masculine in origin as a king's name.

sudat.why_not: Means 'a handsome tooth' — funny and weak as a name.

sudasa.why_not: Contains dāsa (servant/slave) to modern ears; unwanted connotation.

sudiv.name: Sudiv
sudiv.meaning: shining brightly; of beautiful heavenly light
sudiv.say_note: Two clean syllables, no clusters; spelling maps directly.
sudiv.collisions: Distinct from common Sudeep/Sudhir; rare in the USA.
sudiv.note: Gives the ready-made nickname Dev, which travels well in America.

sudyut.why_not: The 'dy' cluster and final -t make it unreadable for Americans.

sunala.why_not: A kind of grass, neuter noun, and sounds feminine.

suma.why_not: Suma is an established feminine name in India; also reads as 'sum'.

sumna.why_not: Awkward -mn- cluster and reads feminine next to Sumana/Sumna.

suroha.name: Suroha
suroha.meaning: one of good growth or fine ascent (su + roha, 'rising'); name of a king
suroha.say_note: Every letter is pronounced as written; no tricky sounds.
suroha.collisions: Not in current use; no near-popular clashes.
suroha.note: Root roha ('rising, growth') gives a positive, defensible sense.

suvar.why_not: Americans will read it as 'suave'/'silver'-ish and it is really an adjective form.

surika.why_not: The -ika ending reads distinctly feminine in both Indian and American ears.

sushva.why_not: Grammarian's example word; the -shv- cluster is unpronounceable in English.

suhrid.why_not: Lovely meaning but the -hr- cluster and 'hrid' will be mangled; also feels like a common word for 'friend'.

surta.why_not: Means 'trodden, walked'; weak and ambiguous meaning.

survya.why_not: Obscure ritual adjective ('being in vessels'); unpronounceable cluster.

sisrat.why_not: A participle form, harsh sound, and sounds like 'sister'.

sripa.why_not: Initial sr- cluster is hard for Americans and it reads like 'Sripa/strip'.

sena.why_not: Means 'dependent on another'; also Sena/Seena reads feminine and is a common surname element.

sairya.why_not: Just 'a kind of grass'; also reads as the feminine name Saira.

somila.name: Somila
somila.meaning: relating to soma / the moon; name of a Sanskrit poet
somila.say_note: Simple syllables; Americans say it right on first try.
somila.collisions: Rare; not part of the 1950–95 Indian male name set.
somila.note: Nickname Milo is a nice American-friendly bonus.

soluka.why_not: Obscure poet's name; sounds like 'Soo-loo-ka' nonsense in English.

sosha.why_not: Means 'mixed with salt earth' — negative; also reads feminine.

saujas.why_not: Spelling invites 'SAW-jazz'; adjective form, not used as a name.

saura.name: Saura
saura.meaning: solar, belonging to the sun; a devotee of the sun
saura.say_note: Two syllables; 'au' reads as 'ow', close to correct.
saura.collisions: Distinct from popular Saurabh; rare on its own.
saura.note: Clean solar meaning and a short, modern shape.

saurya.name: Saurya
saurya.say_note: Slight risk of being read as 'Sorry-ah'; usually said correctly.
saurya.collisions: Overlaps in sound with shaurya (valor), which is a positive association but slightly reduces uniqueness.
saurya.note: Sun imagery with a strong, contemporary sound.

sauhma.why_not: Means 'a king of the Suhmas' — a tribal patronymic; -hm- cluster unsayable.

stavat.why_not: A disputed Vedic participle, not a name; clumsy in English.

stoma.name: Stoma
stoma.say_note: St- is natural in English; reads exactly as spelled.
stoma.collisions: Shares shape with the biology term 'stoma', a mild but low-impact overlap.
stoma.note: Vedic hymn-word; crisp and unused as a given name.

stauti.why_not: A verb citation form ('to praise'), not a name.

snehan.why_not: Too close to the feminine Sneha and the common Snehal; not distinctive.

syala.why_not: Means 'brother-in-law' — a kinship term used mockingly in North India.

srutya.why_not: Grammatical adjective meaning 'relating to a road'; the Sr- cluster gets mangled and the meaning is weak.

svaka.why_not: Means merely 'one's own kinsman'; too plain, and reads like a truncated word.

svagni.why_not: The -gn- cluster after sv- is unpronounceable for Americans.

svadu.name: Svadu
svadu.meaning: Sweet, pleasant to the taste; sweetness
svadu.say_note: Two clean syllables; only the initial sv- takes a moment.
svadu.note: A warm, simple vocabulary word; unused as a given name.

svapas.why_not: Reads as English 'swap-ass' — bad nickname risk.

svaryu.why_not: The -ryu ending is awkward for Americans and the word is a Vedic adjective, not a name.

svaru.why_not: Means a sacrificial stake/piece of wood — a weak, object-like meaning.

svamin.why_not: Instantly read as 'Swami'; a title, not a child's name.

svashu.name: Svashu
svashu.say_note: Spelling maps cleanly; no aspirates or retroflexes.
svashu.note: Vedic adjective; fresh and energetic as a name.

svahya.why_not: Ritual adjective ('worthy of an oblation'); -hy- cluster is hard and the sense is not personal.

svishu.why_not: Reads as 'swish-oo'; sounds comic in English.

svara.why_not: Swara is widely used as a girl's name in Marathi families today.

svojas.name: Svojas
svojas.say_note: Rhymes with the familiar pattern of Ojas; easy two beats.
svojas.collisions: Related to but distinct from the common Ojas
svojas.note: Strong Vedic word, essentially unused as a given name.

haleya.name: Haleya
haleya.meaning: Name of a king in the Bhagavata Purana
haleya.say_note: Phonetic for English readers; stress falls naturally on the middle.
haleya.collisions: Slight echo of 'Haley' — check that the family is fine with it
haleya.note: A genuine puranic royal name that is essentially unheard today.

hastin.why_not: Means elephant/having hands; sounds like 'hasten' and is a known old epic name.

hasas.why_not: Reads as 'hassas'; clumsy and easily mispronounced.

hitvan.why_not: Front-loads the English word 'hit'; reads as 'hit van'.

hijja.why_not: Obscure tree name; the spelling looks odd and invites mispronunciation.

hilla.why_not: Reads as 'Hilla' (Hillary/hill); a bird term with no name value.

hiroka.name: Hiroka
hiroka.say_note: Completely phonetic; every sound exists in English.
hiroka.collisions: Faint resemblance to Japanese Hiro; still clearly Indian in context
hiroka.note: An attested poet's name, attractive and vanishingly rare.

hridya.why_not: The Hr- cluster is mangled by Americans and Hridya reads as a girl's name in India.

hrishi.why_not: Hr- cluster is hard, and it is too close to the very common Hrishikesh/Rishi.

hrishu.why_not: Same Hr- pronunciation problem; Americans say 'hree-shoo' at best.

hema.why_not: Hema is strongly a woman's name in India.

heli.name: Heli
heli.say_note: Very easy; note it may be heard as 'Haley' unless the HAY-lee stress is given.
heli.collisions: Sound-alike with Haley/Heli- prefix; family should be comfortable
heli.note: A Sanskrit word for the sun cognate with Greek helios — a nice bicultural link.

hotri.why_not: A priestly office title, and Americans would read it as 'hot-ree'.

hrada.why_not: Hr- cluster is unpronounceable for Americans.

hradin.why_not: Same Hr- problem; also a descriptive term for a river, not a person.

akara.why_not: Means simply 'the letter a'; no substance as a name.

arinin.why_not: 'Free from debt' is an accounting sense; the repeating -in-in is clumsy.

amsala.why_not: Glossed 'lusty'; the -sala ending also reads feminine in English.

akalka.name: Akalka
akalka.meaning: Free from impurity; pure, without blemish
akalka.say_note: All English-friendly sounds; the -lk- is like 'talk-a'.
akalka.note: Clean virtue meaning with an unusual, memorable shape.

agarva.name: Agarva
agarva.say_note: Reads exactly as spelled for an American; hard g.
agarva.note: A real word with a genuinely appealing virtue meaning, unused as a name.

aguna.why_not: Literally 'without qualities'; reads to laypeople as 'lacking merit', and sounds like 'a goona'.

aguru.name: Aguru
aguru.meaning: Light, not heavy; also the fragrant agarwood
aguru.say_note: Simple open syllables; hard g throughout.
aguru.collisions: Contains 'guru', which Americans will recognize positively
aguru.note: Agarwood is a classical fragrance word — warm, sensory, and unused as a boy's name.

agniya.name: Agniya
agniya.meaning: Belonging to Agni; of the sacred fire
agniya.say_note: The -gn- is read as in 'magnet', which is close enough to correct.
agniya.collisions: Distinct from Agnivesh/Agnay; Agniya is used as a girl's name in Russia, minor overlap
agniya.note: Fire imagery with a soft, modern three-beat sound.

agraga.name: Agraga
agraga.meaning: one who goes in front; a leader
agraga.say_note: Simple open syllables; the repeated -ga can feel sing-song but is read correctly.
agraga.note: Clean vocabulary word meaning leader; slightly repetitive rhythm is the only drawback.

agraja.name: Agraja
agraja.say_note: All light open syllables, no aspirates or retroflexes.
agraja.collisions: Rare; Agraj occurs occasionally in Hindi belt
agraja.note: Well suited to a first child; AJ is a natural American nickname.

agrani.name: Agrani
agrani.meaning: foremost, one who takes the lead
agrani.say_note: Reads phonetically; retroflex n is naturally softened in American English without harm.
agrani.collisions: Used as a Hindi common noun, rarely as a name
agrani.note: Strong, dignified meaning in everyday Marathi/Hindi vocabulary too.

agrapa.why_not: Means 'drinking first' — trivial and odd as a personal name.

agriya.name: Agriya
agriya.meaning: foremost, principal, of the best quality
agriya.say_note: Vedic word that maps cleanly onto English letters.
agriya.collisions: Essentially unused as a given name
agriya.note: Rigvedic pedigree, rare, and yields the friendly nickname Ari.

agreni.why_not: Reads as 'a-GREE-nee', feminine-sounding in English, and duplicates Agrani.
agreni.note: Rejected; Agrani is the better form.

agraha.why_not: In modern Marathi/Hindi agraha means insistence/obstinacy; the dictionary entry is itself disputed.

ankara.why_not: Identical to the Turkish capital and means 'diminution' — weak and confusing.

angaraj.name: Angaraj
angaraj.meaning: king of Anga — an epithet of Karna in the Mahabharata
angaraj.say_note: Final -raj is familiar to Americans; no aspirates.
angaraj.collisions: Recognized epithet, not a common given name
angaraj.note: Carries Karna's heroic, generous associations; Raj is an easy nickname.

angati.why_not: Obscure lexical word for fire; -ati ending sounds feminine in English.

achala.why_not: Achal is a common name for Indian men born 1950–1995, and the -a form reads feminine.

ajara.name: Ajara
ajara.say_note: Three easy syllables; no cluster an American can miss.
ajara.collisions: Rare as a given name; a village name exists
ajara.note: Positive Vedic epithet meaning forever young.

ajira.name: Ajira
ajira.note: Bright, active meaning; masculine in Sanskrit gender.

anjasa.name: Anjasa
anjasa.say_note: No aspirates or retroflexes; nj is natural in English.
anjasa.collisions: Unused as a name; distinct from the popular Anjali
anjasa.note: Rare word with a clean character-based meaning.

atasa.why_not: Reads as a feminine name in English and is an obscure lexicon-only word for wind.

adikka.why_not: Means 'banished from beneath the sky' — strongly negative.

adina.why_not: Identical to the established Hebrew girls' name Adina.

admani.why_not: Reads as 'ad-man' plus -i; awkward in English and obscure.

anagni.why_not: Means 'non-fire', a technical negation with no positive sense.

anala.why_not: Opens to an unfortunate English reading and is also used as a girls' name.

anali.why_not: Same unfortunate English reading; also just a tree name.

anada.why_not: Means 'absence of sound', a phonetic technical term; also confusable with Ananda.

anila.why_not: Common older-generation name and widely used as a girls' name (Aneela/Anila).

anutka.why_not: Harsh -tka cluster and 'self-complacent' shading; reads oddly in English.

anvriju.why_not: The vr- cluster is unpronounceable for Americans.

apeta.why_not: Means 'departed, gone away' — inauspicious for a child.

apusha.why_not: Obscure and invites unpleasant English wordplay.

abjada.why_not: Literally 'lotus-leaf eater'; also collides with Arabic 'abjad'.

amarta.name: Amarta
amarta.say_note: Stress falls naturally on the middle syllable; nothing to mangle.
amarta.note: Rigvedic word; gives the warm nickname Amar without being the common name Amar itself.

amrita.why_not: Overwhelmingly a girls' name in Indian-American usage.

ambuda.name: Ambuda
ambuda.say_note: Fully phonetic; only the initial 'a' may be said as 'am' rather than 'um'.
ambuda.note: Poetic monsoon imagery, masculine in Sanskrit.

amlana.name: Amlan
amlana.say_note: Two clean syllables; the -a form is dropped as is usual in the north and west.
amlana.collisions: Occurs in Bengal; very rare among Marathi families in the US
amlana.note: Elegant meaning of never fading; short and crisp for American ears.

ayavat.why_not: Obscure single-citation word; the -vat ending sounds clipped and odd.

ayama.why_not: This entry means 'not a path' — negative, and it collides with the girls' name Ayama/Ayana.

ayasya.name: Ayasya
ayasya.say_note: Three open syllables; the -sy- cluster is the only speed bump but reads cleanly.
ayasya.collisions: Vaguely near Aayush/Ayaan but distinct in sound and ending
ayasya.note: A Vedic epithet of vigor; unusual and clearly masculine in Rigvedic usage.

ayogin.why_not: Means 'separated from a beloved' — sad, negative meaning.

arajas.name: Arajas
arajas.meaning: dustless; free from passion, serene and pure
arajas.say_note: All simple consonants; Americans read it correctly on sight.
arajas.collisions: Near Arjun only in first letters; no real clash
arajas.note: A philosophical virtue word from the Upanishadic layer — clean, unused as a given name.

arajan.why_not: Literally 'not a king' — a negation, weak meaning.

arusha.why_not: Too close to the child's current name Aarush and to the very popular Aarush/Arush.

arjuna.why_not: Extremely common established name and a standard older-generation name; not unique.

arnoda.name: Arnoda
arnoda.say_note: Stressed long O in the middle makes it easy and memorable for Americans.
arnoda.collisions: No common Indian or English name clash
arnoda.note: Nature imagery of the rain cloud that gives water — generous and vivid.

alaja.why_not: Just 'a kind of bird' with no known positive association; also reads feminine.

alara.why_not: A plant term that reads as a feminine name in the USA (Alara/Lara).

avasa.name: Avasa
avasa.collisions: Slight echo of Avinash/Avi but distinct
avasa.note: Lexical word for 'king'; also shares the root av- 'to protect'. Confirm the parents like the Avi nickname.

avayu.why_not: 'Without wind' — a negation with no value as a name.

avarya.why_not: A technical locational adjective ('on the near bank'); no name value.

avikshit.why_not: Ends in an English obscenity sound ('-shit'); guaranteed bad nickname.

avitri.why_not: Reads distinctly feminine in English (like Avitri/Savitri).

avisha.name: Avisha
avisha.say_note: Easy; the only risk is Americans hearing a softer 'Avisha' as unisex.
avisha.collisions: Avisha is occasionally used for girls in India — worth weighing
avisha.note: Masculine in Monier-Williams ('the ocean'), but the -isha ending can read unisex in the USA.

avela.why_not: Means concealment of knowledge — negative; also reads feminine.

ashira.why_not: Reads feminine (and is a Hebrew girl's name); meaning 'consumer' is unappealing.

ashvayus.why_not: Clumsy -yus ending Americans will mangle; obscure king's name.

ashvala.name: Ashvala
ashvala.meaning: name of the learned Hotri priest of King Janaka; 'of horses'
ashvala.say_note: Reads phonetically; 'shv' is a smooth cluster in English.
ashvala.note: Carries a scholarly Brihadaranyaka association plus the horse root — strong and unused.

asanga.name: Asanga
asanga.say_note: Transparent spelling; Americans say it right the first time.
asanga.collisions: Name of the great Yogachara master Asanga; rare among Indian-American babies
asanga.note: A real historical name with genuine philosophical weight and no modern popularity.

asaman.why_not: 'Without a song' — negation; also reads as 'a saman/a man'.

asura.why_not: In all later usage means demon — unacceptable connotation.

asurya.why_not: Same demon association as Asura; also reads as 'without sun'.

astaka.why_not: Means going to one's final home, i.e. dying — inauspicious.

asvara.why_not: Means 'indistinct, not loud' — a negation, poor meaning.

ahura.why_not: Means 'fire in the stomach' (indigestion-adjacent) and reads as Zoroastrian Ahura Mazda.

amkriti.why_not: Awkward -mkr- cluster and an -i ending that reads feminine; it is a variant reading only.

angeya.name: Angeya
angeya.meaning: a prince of the Anga country
angeya.say_note: Hard G and a clear 'gay' syllable; easy but check the parents are fine with that sound.
angeya.note: Patronymic-style epic word evoking the Anga royal line (Karna's kingdom).

ajadya.why_not: A caste/tribe technical term from Panini; no name value and clumsy -dy- reading.

adipta.name: Adipta
adipta.say_note: The long 'deep' syllable anchors it; Americans read it perfectly.
adipta.collisions: Related to but clearly distinct from the common Dipak/Deepak
adipta.note: Same dip- root as Deepak but fresh; 'Adi' is a natural, warm short form.

adyota.name: Adyota
adyota.say_note: The dy- onset needs one hearing but the stressed YO keeps it clear.
adyota.collisions: Echoes the common Jyoti (feminine) only in root, not in sound
adyota.note: From the dyut root 'to shine'; masculine noun, entirely unused as a given name.

amanju.why_not: Contains Manju, a common feminine Indian name; reads feminine.

amodin.why_not: The usable form Amod is a common older-generation Marathi men's name; Amodin is an awkward stem.

amnata.why_not: A grammatical participle ('quoted, handed down'); weak as a name and the mn- cluster is awkward.

aradvat.why_not: Clunky -dvat ending Americans will stumble over; obscure with no transparent meaning.

arama.name: Arama
arama.meaning: delight, pleasure; also a pleasure-garden or grove
arama.say_note: Fully phonetic and melodic for American speakers.
arama.collisions: Contains 'Rama' visually; in Hindi/Urdu aaram also means rest/comfort
arama.note: Lovely garden-and-delight imagery; the parents should be comfortable with the everyday Hindi sense 'rest, comfort'.

ardraka.why_not: Ardraka literally means 'ginger'; also awkward 'drk' cluster for Americans.

alinga.why_not: Means 'a kind of drum'; contains 'linga', which invites unwanted associations.

aluka.why_not: Also means 'potato' in common Indian usage; comic.

avanta.name: Avanta
avanta.meaning: a king of Avanti, the ancient realm of Ujjain
avanta.collisions: Close to the place-name Avanti and to 'Avantika' (feminine)
avanta.note: Masculine form, clearly distinct from the girl's name Avantika.

avala.why_not: Means a water basin around a tree trunk; weak meaning and reads as 'a-vala'/feminine.

avitin.why_not: A ritual technical term for a thread-wearer; not a name, and meaning is obscure.

ashara.why_not: Too close to Ashara/Ashura and to girls' name Ashara; also reads feminine.

ashuga.name: Ashuga
ashuga.say_note: All open syllables; Americans read it correctly.
ashuga.note: Nice 'swift as the wind' sense, epithet of wind and arrow.

ashmana.why_not: Reads as 'Ash-man'; awkward English nickname and an obscure epithet.

ahvriti.why_not: 'hvr' cluster is unpronounceable for Americans; -i ending reads feminine.

ikara.why_not: Means merely 'the letter i'; a grammatical term, not a name.

ivarna.why_not: Grammatical term for the vowel i; meaningless as a name.

indrota.name: Indrota
indrota.meaning: upheld or promoted by Indra; name of a Vedic teacher
indrota.say_note: Reads cleanly; 'droh' is easy for English speakers.
indrota.note: Genuine Rigvedic personal name, essentially unused today.

ilisha.why_not: Means a kind of fish; also reads as the feminine name Ilisha/Alisha.

ilvala.why_not: Ilvala is a demon in the Mahabharata (and a fish); negative association.

ishira.name: Ishir
ishira.say_note: Dropping the final -a gives a crisp masculine two-syllable name.
ishira.collisions: Ishir is close to Ishaan/Ishir but far rarer
ishira.note: Vedic adjective for vigor; the -a form would read feminine, so Ishir is preferred.

ukara.why_not: Grammatical term for the letter u; no real meaning as a name.

ujjivin.name: Ujjivin
ujjivin.meaning: one who lives fully, reviving, thriving
ujjivin.say_note: Double j is read correctly; ends like 'Kevin'.
ujjivin.collisions: Related to the common word ujjivan (revival)
ujjivin.note: Also a counsellor character in the Panchatantra.

utkuja.why_not: Obscure word for a cooing sound; 'kuja' invites mangling and odd readings.

uttapa.why_not: Means 'great heat'; also reads like the dish 'uttapam'.

uttama.why_not: A very common older-generation name/word meaning 'best'; not unique.

uttala.name: Uttal
uttala.say_note: Short and phonetic; dropping final -a avoids a feminine look.
uttala.note: Used in classical poetry for towering waves and strength.

utsada.why_not: Also means 'excess/swelling, destruction' in other senses; ambiguous and reads oddly.

utsura.why_not: Means sunset time; also 'a-sura' echo and weak sense for a name.

udarka.name: Udarka
udarka.meaning: resounding; also the future, the happy result to come
udarka.note: Rigvedic word; doubles as 'sound rising' and 'good result'.

uddaha.why_not: Means burning/fire; aspirated 'dh'-like cluster and harsh meaning.

udbala.name: Udbal
udbala.say_note: db cluster is mild; reads cleanly as ood-bahl.

udroka.name: Udroka
udroka.say_note: Easy open syllables, stress falls naturally.
udroka.note: Rare literary word; unmistakably unused as a name.

upabda.why_not: 'bd' cluster is unpronounceable for Americans; means mere 'noise'.

upadya.why_not: Means 'second/next'; a grammatical ordinal, weak meaning.

urana.why_not: Means 'ram, sheep'; also reads feminine and close to Urana/Uranus.

urasa.name: Uras
urasa.say_note: Two clean syllables; final -a dropped to avoid a feminine look.
urasa.note: Connotes courage and a broad heart.

ulupa.why_not: Means a kind of grass; also evokes Ulupi, a female Mahabharata character.

ulbana.why_not: Primary sense is the fetal membrane / 'excessive'; unpleasant meaning.

ullopya.why_not: Technical term for a song type; -ya ending and 'lop' are awkward in English.

ushira.name: Ushir
ushira.note: Classical fragrance imagery from Sanskrit poetry.

usriya.why_not: 'sr' cluster plus -iya ending is hard for Americans and reads feminine.

uvarna.why_not: Grammatical term for the letter u; no name value.

urjayat.name: Urjayat
urjayat.meaning: filled with energy and vigor; name of a teacher
urjayat.say_note: 'Urj' is readable; stress on first syllable.
urjayat.collisions: Shares root with the common name Urja (feminine)
urjayat.note: Masculine form with a strong energy meaning and a nice 'Jay' nickname.

rikara.why_not: Means only 'the letter ṛ' — a grammarian's term, no real meaning for a person

ritaja.name: Ritaja
ritaja.meaning: born of cosmic truth and order; of a true nature
ritaja.say_note: Spelling is fully phonetic; no aspirates or retroflex traps
ritaja.collisions: Echoes the common Rita/Ritika family but stands apart as a boy's name
ritaja.note: Rooted in ṛta, the Vedic concept of truth and cosmic order — strong, meaningful and essentially unused.

ritodya.why_not: Reads as 'rit-ODD-ya' to Americans and is an abstract neuter noun, not name-like

ritujit.name: Ritujit
ritujit.meaning: conqueror of the seasons; name of a king of Mithila
ritujit.say_note: Every syllable reads as written; ends crisply
ritujit.note: Ritu is more often a girl's element in Hindi, but the -jit ending makes it clearly masculine.

rikshoda.why_not: The 'ksh' cluster is unpronounceable for Americans and it is just a mountain's name

rijuyu.why_not: Vowel pile-up is awkward and unspellable in the USA

ridupa.why_not: Obscure adjective 'drinking what is sweet'; reads oddly and sounds unfinished

ekara.why_not: Just the name of the letter 'e' — no usable meaning

ekaja.name: Ekaja
ekaja.meaning: born alone; unique, one of a kind
ekaja.say_note: Simple open syllables; no cluster or aspirate
ekaja.collisions: Shares the Ek- element with Ekansh, but that ending is avoided here
ekaja.note: Vedic word; a natural fit for an only child but fine regardless.

ekaraj.name: Ekaraj
ekaraj.meaning: shining alone; sole sovereign, the one who alone is visible
ekaraj.say_note: Ends in 'raj', already familiar to American ears
ekaraj.collisions: Not to be confused with the common surname element Raj
ekaraj.note: Bhagavata usage; dignified and virtually unused as a given name.

ekagni.why_not: The 'gni' cluster defeats American readers and the meaning ('one and the same fire') is ritual jargon

enanka.name: Enanka
enanka.say_note: Reads cleanly; only risk is a flat first 'e', easily corrected
enanka.collisions: No clash with common moon names like Chandra or Indu
enanka.note: A poetic classical epithet of the moon, masculine in Sanskrit.

etagva.why_not: The -gva ending is unsayable and the word is an obscure Vedic horse epithet

etavat.why_not: Purely a grammatical quantifier ('so much'), not a name

eranga.why_not: Means a kind of fish; also reads like an African place name

evasha.why_not: Means 'a kind of small animal' and looks feminine in English

aikara.why_not: Name of a letter only; meaningless as a personal name

okara.why_not: Name of a letter; also reads as 'okra' in the USA

aukara.why_not: Name of a letter; no meaning and an odd spelling

aurasa.why_not: Technical term for a chest-produced sound; reads as 'oral' and looks feminine

kakara.why_not: Name of the letter 'ka'; the kaka- opening invites bathroom teasing

kankana.why_not: In ordinary usage means 'bangle' and reads as a girl's name

kamjaja.why_not: The mj cluster and doubled -ja-ja are clumsy in English

kanina.why_not: Classically means a son born to an unmarried girl; also reads as a feminine name

kandala.why_not: A neuter flower word, feminine-sounding, and too close to English 'scandal/candle'

kapindra.why_not: 'Lord of monkeys' invites teasing in an American school

kapivat.why_not: 'Monkey-possessing' sage name; awkward meaning and clipped ending

karanin.why_not: Bare teacher's name with no clear meaning; ending is weak

karija.why_not: Means 'young elephant'; reads as a girl's name in the USA

karusha.why_not: Name of an antagonist king/tribe; also sounds like a feminine 'Karisha'

kardana.why_not: Only a bare prince's name with no transparent meaning, and it reads like 'cardigan/Cardenas'

karmajit.name: Karmajit
karmajit.meaning: conqueror of karma; one who masters action
karmajit.say_note: 'Karma' is already an English word, so Americans read it instantly
karmajit.collisions: Slight Punjabi-Sikh flavour from the -jit ending, but pan-Indian in Sanskrit
karmajit.note: A royal name in the Bhagavata Purana; strong philosophical meaning.

kavindu.name: Kavindu
kavindu.meaning: moon among poets; an epithet of Valmiki
kavindu.say_note: Every sound exists in English; no cluster or aspirate
kavindu.collisions: Distinct from the common Kavin/Kavish names
kavindu.note: Combines kavi (poet) and indu (moon) — literary and lyrical, essentially unused.

kakayu.why_not: Name of a creeping plant; the kaka- opening also invites teasing

katara.why_not: As a common word kātara means 'cowardly, faint-hearted'; also a fish and the country Qatar

katala.why_not: Means a species of carp; no dignity as a name

kapila.why_not: A well-established older-generation name for Indian men and also used for women; not unique

kamada.why_not: The kāma- opening reads as 'desire/Kama Sutra' to Americans; also used as a goddess epithet

kamyaka.name: Kamyaka
kamyaka.meaning: the desirable, beautiful one; name of the forest where the Pandavas lived in exile
kamyaka.say_note: The 'my' glide takes one correction, then it is stable
kamyaka.collisions: No collision with current Indian-American baby names
kamyaka.note: Evocative Mahabharata forest with a clean adjectival meaning 'desirable'.

karttika.why_not: A month name and too close to the very common Kartik/Karthik

kashisha.why_not: Obscure epithet 'lord of the Kashis'; reads awkwardly and sounds feminine (-isha/-sha).

kashika.why_not: Merely a prince's name variant; sounds feminine and close to Kashika/Kanishka confusion.

kashiya.why_not: A variant reading of a dynastic label, not a usable name; sounds feminine.

kikivi.why_not: Means 'a kind of bird'; sounds like baby-talk and feminine.

kimdatta.why_not: Name of a well; 'kim' (what) gives a nonsense/odd meaning.

kikasa.why_not: Means 'hard, firm' but also vertebra/bone; awkward and odd-sounding.

kilala.name: Kilal
kilala.meaning: a sweet heavenly drink akin to nectar (amrita)
kilala.say_note: Simple vowels; Kilal avoids the feminine-sounding final -a.
kilala.note: Vedic word for a divine sweet beverage; fresh and easy for Americans.

kupilu.why_not: Name of a poisonous ebony tree; 'ku-' prefix and 'pee-loo' sound are unattractive.

kushanku.why_not: Obscure prince name; clumsy sound, Americans would mangle it.

kupapa.why_not: Though glossed 'the sun', it contains 'papa' (sin/father) and sounds comical.

kunala.name: Kunal
kunala.meaning: a kind of bird; also borne by Ashoka's son Kunala
kunala.say_note: Easy, but note it is the familiar name Kunal.
kunala.collisions: Very common among Indian men born 1970-1995
kunala.note: Real and pleasant but fails the uniqueness/older-generation test in practice; include only if parents accept a familiar name.

kuntijit.why_not: 'Conqueror of Kunti' — odd meaning, harsh final cluster.

kupata.why_not: Corrupt dictionary entry / adverb; not a name.

kuraba.name: Kurav
kuraba.say_note: Plain consonants; stress on second syllable.
kuraba.collisions: Rare; not a current baby name
kuraba.note: Kurabaka/kurava is a classical flowering shrub; homonym with 'bad-voiced' kurava is a caveat, so Kuraba spelling may be safer.

kururaj.why_not: Epithet of Duryodhana — negative epic association.

kurunga.why_not: Obscure Vedic prince; -unga ending sounds odd in English.

kulapa.name: Kulap
kulapa.meaning: chief or protector of the family or clan
kulapa.collisions: Not in use as a name
kulapa.note: Vedic word for clan-protector; a strong, defensible meaning for a first son.

kulaka.why_not: 'Chief of a guild' but also a technical term for a group of verses; sounds slight.

kulaha.why_not: Means a horse of a certain colour; ending -aha is awkward.

kuvama.why_not: Commentarial gloss only for 'sun'; 'ku-' and 'vama' read poorly.

kuvaya.why_not: Just 'a kind of bird'; weak, feminine-sounding.

kushiti.why_not: Obscure teacher's name; 'kusIda/kusita' overtones and feminine ending.

kushika.name: Kushik
kushika.meaning: name of a prince, ancestor of the Kaushika line (from kusha, sacred grass)
kushika.say_note: Reads cleanly; rhymes with 'Kaushik' but distinct.
kushika.collisions: Close to the common Kaushik — a caveat
kushika.note: Father of Vishvamitra's line; dignified and easy, though family should weigh Kaushik similarity.

kushidin.why_not: Variant of a teacher's name; kusida means 'usury/lazy' — negative.

kustuka.why_not: Obscure teacher's name, no meaning; clumsy sound.

kupara.name: Kupar
kupara.say_note: Easy; risk of being read like 'Cooper'.
kupara.collisions: Unused as a name; near-echo of surname Kapoor
kupara.note: Vedic word for ocean — grand meaning, simple sounds.

kritimat.why_not: Ends in -mat, a grammatical stem form; hard to carry in the USA.

kritvya.why_not: Consonant cluster -tvya is unpronounceable for Americans.

krishana.why_not: Would be read as Krishna/Krishana — collides with the most common name group.

ketaka.name: Ketak
ketaka.collisions: Ketaki is the common girl's name; Ketak is the masculine form and rare
ketaka.note: Marathi-familiar poetic plant; masculine form keeps it boyish and uncommon.

kenipa.name: Kenip
kenipa.say_note: Easy to say; 'nip' ending is slightly abrupt in English.
kenipa.note: Rare Rigvedic word for sage; Ken works as a natural American short form.

kerala.why_not: Reads as the Indian state and is South-Indian specific.

kesharin.name: Kesharin
kesharin.say_note: Three easy syllables; no aspirates or retroflex issues.
kesharin.collisions: Kesari/Kesar known as words; Kesharin rare as a name
kesharin.note: Lion imagery, strong and masculine; Kesarin is also Hanuman's father's name.

kaijava.why_not: Uncertain corrupt teacher's name with no meaning.

kairava.name: Kairav
kairava.meaning: the white lotus that blooms by night
kairava.collisions: Occasionally used, still uncommon in the USA
kairava.note: Beautiful meaning and yields the very American nickname Kai.

kailasa.why_not: Sacred mountain/Shiva's abode — heavy, and common as Kailash for older men.

kaishika.why_not: A raga name but feminine-sounding and too close to Kaushika/Keshika.

kokalla.why_not: Reads oddly, invites 'koala'/'cola' jokes; only an inscriptional king name

kodara.why_not: Means a kind of coarse grain; weak meaning

kauntya.why_not: Grammatical patronymic form; -ntya cluster hard to say

kramajit.name: Kramajit
kramajit.meaning: One who conquers step by step; victorious through method
kramajit.say_note: Initial kr- cluster is easy; all short clean vowels
kramajit.note: Name of a prince in the Mahabharata; distinctive and strong.

kramunja.why_not: Awkward -unja cluster, obscure mountain, sounds invented

kruncha.why_not: Reads as English 'crunch'; a snipe bird

kraivya.why_not: Patronymic of an obscure tribe; -vya hard for Americans

kshamya.why_not: Ksh- start plus -mya is mangled by Americans; reads feminine

kshiraka.why_not: Ksh- spelling is mispronounced; 'milky' feel, too close to Kshira

kshudri.why_not: Looks like kshudra ('petty'); Ksh- cluster unreadable

kshemin.name: Kshemin
kshemin.meaning: One who enjoys peace and security; safe, at ease
kshemin.say_note: Americans will say 'Shemin/Kshemin'; close enough and easy to correct
kshemin.collisions: Related to Kshem/Kshemya but itself unused
kshemin.note: Lovely meaning of wellbeing; slight risk from Ksh- spelling.

kshmaja.why_not: Kshm- cluster is impossible for Americans

ganesha.why_not: Major deity name, extremely common and older-generation

gamika.why_not: Ends in -ika, reads feminine; meaning 'travelling' is weak

gayana.name: Gayan
gayana.collisions: Close to the word gaayan (singing) in Marathi/Hindi; rare as a name
gayana.note: Musical and warm; 'Gayan' spelling avoids a feminine -a ending, though the nickname 'Gay' is a caution.

girisha.why_not: Reads as the common name Girish, typical of men born 1950–1985

guvaka.why_not: Betel-nut tree; awkward sound, no name feel

godari.why_not: Too close to the river name Godavari; adjectival epithet

gomanta.name: Gomanta
gomanta.meaning: Name of a mountain; also 'rich in cattle/possessing herds' i.e. prosperous
gomanta.collisions: Gomantak = Goa, a pleasant Marathi association
gomanta.note: Strong Maharashtra/Konkan resonance (Gomantak) with a mountain in the Mahabharata.

gopika.why_not: Gopika is a well-known girl's name

gautama.why_not: Very common established name, also older-generation (Gautam)

nakara.why_not: Just 'the letter N'; no real meaning for a person

chakshas.name: Chakshas
chakshas.meaning: A teacher, spiritual instructor; related to sight and insight
chakshas.say_note: 'ksh' mid-word is manageable but the final -s is slightly clunky
chakshas.note: Fine meaning of vision and guidance; consider the shorter 'Chaksh' form.

chandra.why_not: Extremely common, older-generation, and a girl's name in the US

chanura.why_not: Chanura was the wrestler-demon killed by Krishna — negative figure

chaluki.why_not: Reads as a dynasty/surname (Chalukya) and ends -i, feminine feel

chitrya.name: Chitrya
chitrya.collisions: Echoes Chitra (a girl's name), but Chitrya itself is unused
chitrya.note: Rigvedic word for brilliant; distinctive but note the Chitra echo.

chettri.why_not: Identical to the Nepali surname Chhetri; not a first name

chipudru.why_not: Obscure tree word, clumsy sound, unpronounceable cluster for Americans.

janana.why_not: Means birth/begetting; reads as a grammatical noun and sounds feminine (Janana/Janani).

janina.why_not: Janina is an established European girls' name; clearly feminine in the USA.

jayashva.why_not: The -shva cluster is unpronounceable for Americans.

jayendra.why_not: A well-used older-generation Indian men's name, not unique.

jalalu.why_not: Bulbous plant; weak meaning and sounds like Arabic Jalal derivatives.

jalhana.why_not: The -lh- cluster is unreadable for Americans.

javina.name: Javin
javina.say_note: Spells itself; rhymes with Kevin/Gavin so Americans read it instantly.
javina.collisions: Echoes Gavin/Javier but is a distinct spelling; very rare among Indian-American babies.
javina.note: From the root jav (to hurry); the -in stem form Javin is the natural masculine name shape.

jananti.why_not: A teacher's name derived from a verb form; reads as a Sanskrit verb ('they know'), not a name.

jambavat.why_not: Name of the epic bear/monkey chief; heavy, dated, and invites 'Jumbo' teasing.

jinashri.why_not: The -shri ending reads feminine in the USA and the 'shr' cluster is hard.

jimuta.name: Jimut
jimuta.say_note: Both vowels are long and unambiguous in English spelling; no clusters.
jimuta.collisions: Close in feel to the common Jimutavahana but not a used baby name today.
jimuta.note: Vedic word for the rain cloud; a fresh alternative to the popular Megh names.

jivada.name: Jivad
jivada.meaning: Life-giver; one who bestows life (a healer)
jivada.collisions: Shares the familiar jiv- element with Jeev/Jivan without being either.

jyautsna.why_not: Consonant pile-up jy-/-tsn- is impossible from English spelling; also feels feminine (Jyotsna).

tadraja.why_not: It is a grammatical term for a suffix; not a name.

tanuna.why_not: 'Bodiless' is an odd meaning for a child and the name reads feminine.

tapita.name: Tapit
tapita.meaning: Refined, purified (as gold tempered by fire)
tapita.say_note: Two open English-friendly syllables; no ambiguity.
tapita.collisions: Distinct from the common Tapan; unused as a baby name.
tapita.note: Participle of tap (to heat/refine), used in the Harivamsa for refined gold.

tamaka.why_not: Means asthma/chest oppression — negative medical term.

tarala.name: Taral
tarala.say_note: Reads cleanly; dropping the final -a avoids a feminine look.
tarala.collisions: Taral/Tarall exists as a rare Gujarati-Marathi name; not popular now.
tarala.note: Masculine noun in the Bhagavata for a wave; the -a-less form Taral is the usual modern shape.

taluna.why_not: Lexical variant of taruna; obscure, reads feminine, and close to Taruna (girl).

tatarya.why_not: Obscure prince name; reads as 'Tatar' plus -ya, no usable meaning.

tapija.why_not: Merely means 'found near the Tapti river'; a geographic adjective, not a name.

taraksha.why_not: Name of a Daitya (demon); negative association despite the pretty meaning.

tarksha.why_not: 'A kind of bird' with uncertain form; harsh cluster and no real meaning to claim.

tasuna.why_not: Means a kind of hemp; weak and feminine-sounding.

tijila.name: Tijil
tijila.say_note: Short clear syllables; no clusters or retroflexes.
tijila.collisions: Essentially unused; no clash with any common name.
tijila.note: Rare lexical word for the moon listed in the Unadi commentary; a fresh alternative to Chandra names.

timita.name: Timit
timita.say_note: Reads phonetically; 'ti-MEET' is the natural American reading.
timita.collisions: Slight echo of Amit/Sumit but distinct and very rare.
timita.note: Used in the Ramayana for 'quiet, unmoving'; the -a-less Timit fits modern usage.

timija.why_not: Adjective for a sort of pearl's origin; obscure and feminine-sounding.

timiri.why_not: Means a kind of fish; also reads feminine and near 'timir' (darkness).

timisha.why_not: The -isha ending reads feminine in the USA; meaning is just an unnamed tree.

tirima.why_not: 'A kind of rice' — trivial meaning, feminine sound.

turvasha.name: Turvash
turvasha.meaning: Name of a Rigvedic hero and ancestral chieftain (from tur-, swift/overpowering)
turvasha.say_note: Two syllables, both spelled as read; 'sh' is safe for Americans.
turvasha.collisions: Distinct from the -aansh trend; not in use as a baby name.
turvasha.note: Turvasha (Turvasu) is named with Yadu in the Rigveda as an Aryan progenitor.

tulaka.name: Tulak
tulaka.meaning: One who weighs and considers; a king's counsellor
tulaka.note: From tul (to weigh/ponder); attested in the Divyavadana for a royal advisor.

tulya.why_not: Reads as English 'tool' at the start and is mainly a grammatical adjective ('equal').

tutuma.why_not: Sing-song reduplication that sounds comic in English.

trinanku.why_not: The tr- plus nasal cluster and retroflex make it unreadable for Americans.

taittiri.why_not: Double-t spelling and -iri ending; Americans will mangle it and it sounds feminine.

tolaka.why_not: Means a unit of weight (tola); a measurement, not a name.

taulvali.why_not: Awkward -lv- cluster and no meaning beyond an obscure teacher's patronymic.
